question: Can the Palawan marine/inland fish checklist in Balisco's 2024 dissertation or its 2023 marine article support a public, waterbody-resolved species batch?

studyScope.dissertationMetadata: National Sun Yat-sen University catalog identifies Rodulf Anthony Balisco's 290-page English PhD dissertation, submitted 2024-08-08 and examined 2024-07-10. Its contents list separate marine and inland-fish chapters, a Puerto Princesa Subterranean River chapter, and a Palawan fish checklist appendix beginning on page 249.
studyScope.marineArticleReportedScope: Balisco et al. (2023) reports 1,056 marine fishes compiled from UVC surveys conducted during 2003-2021 and published literature across 156 sites and 25 locations in the Sulu Sea and West Philippine Sea. It is a marine component and remains separate from the broader dissertation aggregate.

integrityFindings.abstractCountConflict: The dissertation abstract first reports 155 species described from Palawan waters, then states that 156 valid species have been described from Palawan waters. This internal difference is unresolved.
integrityFindings.habitatCountInterpretation: The abstract reports 1,547 marine and 138 inland-water species alongside a total of 1,647. It does not establish that habitat categories are disjoint; do not add or subtract these counts to infer a corrected total.
integrityFindings.waterbodyCrosswalk: The catalog abstract and table of contents do not expose species-by-waterbody rows, sample dates, collection methods per taxon, voucher identifiers, accession crosswalks, or coordinates. The checklist appendix is listed but was not inspected.
integrityFindings.dissertationAccess: The official catalog links a full-text PDF but routes the file link to a separate download page with required input fields. No file was downloaded. The record permits off-campus reading but limits the full text to personal, noncommercial research/search/reading/printing and prohibits reproduction, distribution, modification, reposting, and broadcast.
integrityFindings.articleAccess: The publisher page exposes the marine article abstract and displays a purchase-PDF path. No item-specific open license or public-app reuse permission was verified.
integrityFindings.currentPresence: Both works compile historical material and surveys; the 2023 marine sampling window ends in 2021. Neither provides real-time presence, catchability, current abundance, fishing rules, or safety status.

limits: Abstract aggregates are not a checked checklist and cannot be projected into Palawan waterbodies or municipal fishing areas.
The 2023 marine article's 1,056-species aggregate must not be merged with the dissertation's 1,647 total or treated as 1,056 current site detections.
The dissertation's terms do not authorize copying or modifying its appendix into a public application; written rights-holder permission would be required for that reuse.
The full dissertation and its appendix were not retrieved; the direct download flow was not completed.
Marine, inland-water, subterranean-river, and market/landing evidence must remain distinct until the full methods and source crosswalk are reviewed.

followUp.nextAction: Use the abstract and catalog only as a high-priority Palawan coverage lead. Continue with openly accessible Palawan sources whose license permits reuse, beginning with the NFRDI Palawan cartilaginous-fish checklist; consider asking for rights clearance only after Joseph decides he wants to use this dissertation's appendix.
